angle: Executives’ fear shows up as control theater—scope thrash, consensus traps, and value delays.
linkedinPost:
Most AI programs don’t die from bad models—they die from leadership anxiety.

MIT Sloan Management Review describes how transformation efforts derail when leaders manage their fears instead of the work: constant re-scoping, performative updates, and decision bottlenecks.

From the trenches, I see three telltales:
- Consensus traps: “Let’s get ten VPs to align” (translation: no owner).
- Control theater: new steering decks every week while teams wait on access.
- Scope thrash: redefining success mid-flight to avoid committing to outcomes.

My fixes are boring and effective:
- Name a single accountable exec. Publish 3 metrics and freeze them for a quarter.
- Time-box decisions (72 hours) and pre-commit to default paths if no verdict.
- Move status from slides to telemetry dashboards tied to production usage.

When anxiety is channeled into clarity, throughput jumps. When it isn’t, AI becomes a very expensive group therapy session.

Which anti-pattern above do you see most—and what’s one mechanism you’ll install this month to counter it? #AITransformation #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
